points.description: Establishes that A_n grows slowly/regularly (e.g. A_{n+1}-A_n ∈ {0,1}, A_n → ∞, and A_n ≈ √n so consecutive values change by at most 1 and take every positive integer value), and states a useful lemma of this type (such as: for every large k there are n with A_n = k, and the interval of n with A_n=k is long/ends where a perfect power occurs).

levels.says: Only observes A_n is slowly increasing / increments by 0 or 1, without a usable lemma or proof.

points.description: Sets up a discrete intermediate value argument: considers a quantity like f(n) = (n+2024) mod A_n, or compares n+2024 with multiples k·A_n, and shows it moves from at-or-below to at-or-above the target as n varies (e.g. the ratio (n+2024)/A_n changes by controlled steps, so it must hit an integer).

levels.says: Sets up the idea but the step-size control is incomplete or incorrectly justified.

points.description: Completes the argument rigorously: shows that for arbitrarily large values (e.g. each large k) there is an n with A_n | n+2024, and that these n are distinct/unbounded, giving infinitely many.

levels.says: Finds solutions but does not justify rigorously that there are infinitely many, or has a gap in the final step.

points.description: Correct, complete write-up: all bounds on A_n (such as counting perfect powers by squares, cubes, etc., or the needed estimate) are justified, with no unproved key claims.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a complete proof that uses slow growth of A_n and a discrete intermediate-value-style argument to get infinitely many n. Part marks for noting A_n increases slowly with a lemma, or for using the intermediate value idea without finishing. Alternative correct proofs earn full marks.
